coverage_policy: every non-empty normative source line in Sections 1-21, plus both owner-approved amendments

rules.summary: The workflow exists to move an owner-authorized product outcome from intake to verified delivery, safe operation, and eventual retirement without role confusion, duplicate authority, hidden state, silent failure, or unverifiable completion.
The workflow conforms only when all of the following are true:
1. Every state-changing action has one authenticated actor, one named command, one exact target, one current policy version, and one durable receipt.
2. No later flow invents authority that an earlier flow did not grant.
3. One authoritative work-item card remains stable while attempts, incidents, releases, and generations remain linked records beneath it.
4. A process, heartbeat, report, command exit code, stopped alert, or UI label never proves success by itself.
5. Completion, restoration, deployment health, and retirement are independently verified from authoritative state.
6. Product, project, workspace, environment, artifact, and resource identities fail closed on ambiguity.
7. Every agent follows its role contract and orientation; personality guidance never expands authority.
8. The system improves outcomes rather than rewarding activity volume, vanity metrics, or automatic punishment.

The implementation MUST provide these logically distinct components. A deployment MAY combine processes only when identity, credentials, permissions, logging, and failure boundaries remain independently enforceable.
| Component | Normative responsibility | Forbidden authority |

| Guarded Command Service | Sole durable workflow-state writer; validates identity, capability, policy, lease, fencing, idempotency, and preconditions | Free-form commands, direct product implementation, silent policy expansion |
| Durable Ledger | Append-only accepted command, event, decision, incident, evidence, and effect receipts | Mutable history, secret storage, inferred approval |
| Signed Policy Registry | Versioned authority, classifier, lens, recovery, severity, timing, retention, resource, and security contracts | Incident-time self-expansion |
| Capability Service | Issues short-lived exact-action capabilities and revokes them by epoch | Broad reusable or cross-product authority |
| Lease and Resource Scheduler | Exclusive leases, fair queues, durable wait tokens, trusted wake-up, priority and precedence | Busy retry loops or unrecorded queue bypass |
| Product Watchdog | Read-only invariant, liveness, progress, dependency, and service observation | Diagnosis, mutation, recovery, card movement |
| Recovery Executor | Mechanical allowlisted recovery through guarded commands | Diagnosis, implementation, commits, deployment, owner decisions |
| Artifact Registry | Immutable, product-namespaced, content-addressed build artifacts and provenance | Workspace artifacts as release truth |
| Secret Broker | Resolves minimum production secret at execution without exposing raw value | Prompt, card, evidence, log, or standing-worker secret access |
| Evidence Store | Sensitivity-tiered immutable evidence and read-back results | Raw real secrets or unverified mutable claims |
| Evaluation Service | Daily exceptions and weekly trends with root-cause attribution | Automatic punishment, authority, dispatch, or state change |

All persistent workflow mutations MUST pass through the Guarded Command Service. Direct Kanban, ledger, registry, release, incident, or policy writes MUST be rejected, audited, and classified as a security incident. The service MUST accept
- Flow 1 Product Secretary commands;
- Flow 2 Recovery Executor commands;
- Flow 3 Build and Release commands;
- Flow 4 operational, incident, maintenance, and retirement commands;
- cross-flow security-response commands.
The Watchdog MUST remain read-only.
Every durable record MUST use opaque immutable identifiers and explicit parent links:
Product
└── Project / bounded delivery domain
└── WorkItem
├── IntakeAudit
├── DeliveryProfileDecision
├── WorkAttempt
│   ├── WorkerLease
│   ├── EvidencePacket
│   └── RunIncidentGeneration
├── ReviewSet
│   ├── ReviewerVerdict A
│   ├── ReviewerVerdict B
│   └── GatekeeperVerdict
├── ReleaseRecord
│   ├── Artifact
│   ├── PromotionAttempt
│   ├── ReleaseIncidentGeneration
│   └── OperationalHandoff
└── ServiceRecord
├── ObjectiveSet
├── OperationalIncidentGeneration
├── ProblemRecord
├── SecurityCase
└── RetirementRecord
Each event and record MUST carry:
correlation:
product_id: opaque-id
project_id: opaque-id
work_item_id: opaque-id | null
service_id: opaque-id | null
root_cause_id: opaque-id | null
parent_record_type: enum | null
parent_record_id: opaque-id | null
record_type: enum
record_id: opaque-id
generation: integer >= 1 | null
policy_version: semver-or-digest
authority_epoch: integer >= 1
created_at_control_time: monotonic-control-time

Correlation MUST link identities without merging them. A run incident, release incident, operational incident, problem record, and security case MUST retain distinct lifecycle and closure semantics even when they share `root_cause_id`.

Policy, leader, lease, or fencing rotation MUST NOT create a new incident generation. A generation begins only when the authoritative attempt or semantic invariant changes, or the same semantic failure recurs after valid closure. Rolling ha
Every state-changing command MUST conform to:
command:
command_id: opaque-id
idempotency_key: unique-stable-key
command_type: registered-name
actor_role: registered-role
actor_id: opaque-id
product_id: opaque-id
project_id: opaque-id
target_type: registered-record-type
target_id: opaque-id
work_item_id: opaque-id | null
run_id: opaque-id | null
artifact_id: content-address | null
environment_id: opaque-id | null
workspace_id: opaque-id | null
capability_id: opaque-id
policy_version: semver-or-digest
authority_epoch: integer
fencing_epoch: integer | null
lease_ids: [opaque-id]
reason_code: registered-code
precondition_hash: digest
expires_at_control_time: monotonic-control-time
expected_effect_class: read_only | idempotent | reversible | irreversible

The service MUST atomically validate all fields before accepting the command. A repeated `idempotency_key` MUST return the original result. A changed payload under an existing key MUST fail as an integrity violation.

Effect-capable commands MUST recheck disable, hold, capability, lease, policy, and fencing epochs immediately before the external effect. Non-fenceable external effects MUST be reconciled from authoritative target state before retry or clos
This section defines the shared resource and lease namespace, cross-flow priority rules, waiting semantics, and safe preemption boundary required by the whole-product audit.
Every exclusive or capacity-limited resource MUST have a globally unique namespaced identity:
resource://<product-or-shared>/<class>/<provider>/<region>/<name>

Classes include `workspace`, `build-lane`, `release-lane`, `emergency-release-lane`, `test-device`, `database`, `migration-lock`, `runtime`, `maintenance-window`, `restore-target`, `incident-containment`, and `retirement-target`.

A lease MUST bind resource, holder role and identity, product, project, work item or service, command class, issued epoch, expiry, renewable conditions, queue token, and revocation state. Worker time cannot extend authority. Central monoton

Waiting work MUST retain a durable wait token and visible queue position. A trusted release event MUST trigger guarded re-evaluation. It MUST NOT revive a stale process. Eligible work begins as a fresh fenced attempt only after current poli
Signed policy MUST define priority classes. Default precedence is:
1. Safety containment for confirmed active harm;
2. owner-authorized rollback or restoration;
3. signed emergency release or maintenance;
4. scheduled production release or maintenance;
5. verification and restoration drills;
6. routine build, test, research, and background work.

Higher priority MAY preempt only a command that is explicitly cancellable and safely checkpointed. Otherwise it queues. Priority MUST NOT bypass capability, fencing, artifact, owner, verification, or evidence gates. FIFO applies within a pr

The Product Secretary MUST verify product identity before interpreting actionable content. Wrong-product input MUST be rejected before card creation with a typed receipt naming the correct product destination. The system MUST NOT auto-forwa
The Secretary MAY classify only when trusted declared facts match a signed policy row. Otherwise the accountable PM or read-only auditor MUST supply classification evidence.
Every accepted request MUST receive exactly one profile:
1. `research_only` — read-only evidence and PM synthesis;
2. `bounded_implementation` — one approved small slice;
3. `coordinated_implementation` — declared multi-slice dependency graph and integration gate;
4. `design_required` — specification, plan, or UX artifact before implementation;
5. `protected_or_effectful` — specialized gates, compensation, and explicit authority.

Risk and blast radius define smallness; time is secondary. Small work MUST be one product, within policy module limits, and MUST NOT include migration, protected systems, external effects, deployment, material configuration, or uncertain de
Owner gates MUST offer typed choices only:
- approve proposed delivery profile;
- request specification or plan;
- request UX artifact;
- request clarification or reclassification;
- defer;
- reject.
No default is allowed. Silence grants nothing. Free text cannot expand authority.
Run state MUST use orthogonal projections:
run_state:
lifecycle: queued | dispatched | starting | running | terminal
health: healthy | waiting_resource | stalled | lease_lost | superseded
result: none | passed | failed | cancelled | exhausted

The card represents the work item, not a worker attempt. A replacement creates a new run identity and fencing epoch beneath the same authoritative card. Superseded attempts remain history and their late updates MUST be rejected.

An authenticated renewable lease proves presence and authority. Typed milestones prove progress. Heartbeats alone MUST NOT be shown as meaningful progress. The card MUST display current attempt, health, last meaningful milestone, blocker or

Start acknowledgement uses a two-minute pilot, with a signed five-minute exception for known cold starts. Missing acknowledgement opens a typed never-started incident; retry follows recovery class and budget.
Implementer self-verification occurs in Running and MUST include TDD, tests, static checks, acceptance comparison, and evidence assembly. It is not independent Review.
Every implementation requires two independent reviewers. Each MUST submit a sealed attributed verdict before seeing the other. A guarded classifier selects baseline lenses:
- goal and correctness;
- risk and regression.

Signed policy adds specialist lenses from changed components, dependencies, protected subsystems, and risk class. The PM MAY add a justified lens but MUST NOT remove or weaken a mandatory lens. Only the Owner may approve registry or policy

The Gatekeeper validates immutable candidate identity, checklist completion, both reviews, evidence, contradictions, and blocking findings. Outcomes are `PASS`, `PASS_WITH_CONDITIONS`, or `REQUEST_CHANGES`. Only administrative evidence refe
QA MUST receive enumerated journeys, expected results, evidence requirements, responsible reviewer, and pass, fail, or escalation route. “Needs human QA” without this checklist is invalid.
R0 = read-only or recomputable
R1 = proven idempotent
R2 = compensable through a separately authorized named command
R3 = forbidden, irreversible, or unknown

Automatic recovery is limited to eligible R0 and owner-allowlisted R1. The default pilot is one automatic recovery after the initial attempt; signed policy may narrow to zero. R2 requires separate authorization. R3 and unknown are forbidden

Retry MUST use a new run, fencing epoch, scratch scope, exact workspace binding, and reacquired resources. Partial or unknown external effects require authoritative reconciliation before any retry. Compensation is a separate command with it

Flow 3 MUST build once and verify many. The Build Worker creates an immutable content-addressed artifact with provenance, tests, dependency identity, configuration, bill of materials, and signature. A material rebuild creates a new artifact
Production signing MUST use managed non-exportable hardware-backed keys and short-lived per-artifact signing capabilities. Lower environments use separate lower-trust roots.

Production deployment MUST require explicit Owner authorization bound to exact artifact, environment, configuration version, policy version, strategy, time window, and rollback contract. Approval expires and MUST NOT be reused.

Progressive deployment with health gates and automatic pause is the default when supported. Atomic deployment is permitted only when technical unavailability is recorded. A dedicated emergency release lane MAY be reserved, readiness-tested,

Automatic rollback is permitted only for signed preauthorized objective thresholds where rollback is known reversible and collateral risk is bounded. Ambiguous, irreversible, or collateral-risk rollback requires Owner approval every time. F

Flow 3 closes only after deployment, independent production verification, rollback-readiness recheck, durable evidence, and explicit acknowledgement from the Operational Owner named in the service registry. Silence never accepts responsibil

Each service MUST have a versioned owner-approved objective set containing user-facing indicators, targets, error budget, exclusions, criticality, and review triggers. Health MUST combine telemetry, critical journeys, data integrity, depend
Only actionable, typed, deduplicated alerts with an owner, evidence, severity, runbook reference, acknowledgement lease, routing policy, and false-positive target may page.

Verified invariant, objective, user-impact, security, or dependency violation opens one typed operational incident. Severity derives from signed impact, scope, safety, integrity, security, duration, and reversibility rules; uncertainty esca

A named Incident Commander coordinates. Responders diagnose and execute only named scoped commands. The PM owns technical routing. The Secretary coordinates product escalation and approved communication. Owner attention is limited to reserv

Closure requires independent restoration proof, objective read-back, data-integrity checks, residual-risk ownership, follow-up linkage, and explicit closure. Stopped alerts or successful commands are insufficient.
Repeated or severe incidents create a Problem Record. Product change always enters Flow 1. Flow 2 supervises only after authorization.

Flow 4 may directly execute only signed, preclassified, narrow, reversible operational configuration, containment, maintenance, scaling, restoration, or retirement commands. Any material behavior, scope, entitlement, safety, data, schema, a

Backups MUST be encrypted, provenance-linked, sensitivity-tiered, and access-reviewed. Scheduled restoration drills MUST independently prove recovery time, recovery point, data integrity, key access, and service usability. Backup job succes
Retirement is Owner-only. The approval MUST bind:
retirement_approval:
service_id: opaque-id
environment_ids: [opaque-id]
plan_version: digest
resource_ids: [resource-uri]
consumer_inventory_hash: digest
obligation_inventory_hash: digest
data_disposition_plan_hash: digest
credential_revocation_plan_hash: digest
dependency_removal_plan_hash: digest
legal_hold_state: clear | blocked
approved_window: control-time-range
rollback_or_recovery_contract_id: opaque-id
policy_version: digest
owner_decision_id: opaque-id
authority_epoch: integer
revocation_state: active | revoked | expired
A legal hold is a hard veto. Retirement MUST NOT begin while `legal_hold_state=blocked`.

Execution MUST stop new use, notify and migrate consumers, export or dispose data, prove dependency removal, revoke credentials and access, drain traffic, decommission exact resources, and independently verify absence.
Retirement MUST remain open while any consumer, obligation, legal hold, credential, dependency, residual traffic, failed export, unverified deletion, or required archive remains unresolved.
Retained records MAY contain protected key-escrow references and identifiers, recovery-authority metadata, and access evidence. They MUST NOT contain raw keys or prohibited secrets.
Security response is a cross-cutting authority overlay, not a fifth sequential flow.

Any flow MAY open a typed Security Case linked to the originating record. Entry MUST preserve evidence and immediately apply least-disclosure routing. Ordinary flow authority does not become security authority.
Signed security policy MUST name:
- accountable Security Response Authority;
- incident lead and deputy;
- evidence custodian;
- technical PM;
- Product Secretary communication route;
- allowed read, containment, investigation, recovery, and disclosure commands;
- capability scopes and expiry;
- evidence sensitivity and access rules;
- communication approval rules;
- independent closure verifier;
- residual-risk owner;
- hand-back recipient and acceptance requirements.

Closure requires independently verified containment or restoration, preserved evidence, explicit residual-risk ownership, and linked delivery requests for lasting change. Hand-back MUST state current operational state, restrictions, monitor
Every role MUST have a registered identity, mission, allowed commands, forbidden actions, evidence obligations, escalation owner, decision posture, outcome test, and communication guidance.
| Role | Controlling orientation | Outcome test |
| Product Secretary | Product-faithful, routing-precise, boundary-strict | Correct routing, supervised PM commitments, actionable owner decisions |
| Project PM | Goal-oriented, causal, supervisory | Verified product outcome, not ceremonies or ticket closure |
| Auditor / Classifier | Curious, evidence-skeptical, read-only | Reproducible facts, calibrated confidence, correct profile and lenses |
| Implementer | Bounded root-cause, durable-fix, test-driven | Cause and symptom resolved within scope; broader cause proposed, never hidden |
| Reviewers | Checklist-complete, independently adversarial | Artifact and evidence independently challenged through mandatory lenses |
| Gatekeeper | Exact, synthesis-oriented, verdict-disciplined | One evidence-backed typed verdict preserving every material finding |
| QA | User-outcome and reproducibility focused | Enumerated journeys yield reproducible typed results |
| Watchdog | Vigilant, quiet, observational | Early precise detection with low noise and no mutation |
| Recovery Executor | Mechanical, authority-minimal, fail-closed | Exact allowlisted recovery with receipts and read-back |
| Build Worker | Reproducibility and provenance first | One immutable verifiable artifact from declared inputs |
| Release Worker | Precision and blast-radius aware | Exact approved promotion with reconciled effects |
| Production Verifier | Skeptical and user-impact focused | Independent health, journey, integrity, and identity proof |
| Incident Commander | Calm and priority-disciplined | One truthful timeline and conflict-free coordination |
| Incident Responder | Causal, containment-first, evidence-preserving | Harm bounded, state reconciled, scoped repair verified |
| Operational Owner | Stewardship and readiness oriented | Safely operable service with maintained recovery and retirement readiness |
| Security Authority | Least-disclosure and evidence-custody oriented | Contained harm, preserved custody, verified closure, explicit hand-back |
Band-aids, temporary fixes, and symptom masking are prohibited unless explicitly classified as time-limited containment with owner visibility, expiry, and a linked permanent-remediation request.

The Gatekeeper MUST send the PM the typed verdict plus immutable technical evidence annex. The PM MUST add the technical route and a concise, actionable, lossless summary. The Secretary MUST condense only for owner relevance while retaining
The owner brief MUST contain:
1. requested outcome;
2. what was accomplished;
3. user or product impact;
4. verification result;
5. remaining risk or blocker;
6. next action or owner decision.
It SHOULD omit filenames, diffs, hashes, commands, raw logs, and implementation jargon unless requested. No layer may soften a fail, hide risk, change the verdict, or remove accountability.
Incident projections MUST be orthogonal:
incident:
phase: open | acknowledged | recovery_pending | recovering | closed
severity: registered-level
escalation_level: registered-level
recovery_budget_state: available | consuming | exhausted | forbidden
closure_reason: none | verified_resolved | superseded | false_positive | accepted_risk | administratively_dismissed

Only an explicit close event terminates a generation. `accepted_risk` and `administratively_dismissed` MUST NOT claim restoration or release affected work. Only `verified_resolved` proves restoration. A recurrence after valid closure create
`disable_recovery` stops only Recovery Executor authority, revokes capabilities, advances fencing, preserves Watchdog and ledger visibility, and reconciles in-flight effects.

`project_hold` is a separate Owner-authorized command. It MUST bind an immutable exact membership set, request checkpoints, stop new dispatch, and place affected work in truthful typed Blocked state. Resume MUST reference the same hold reco
Product Secretary and release control-plane failover MUST be active-passive. A standby takes over only after reconciliation, obtains a newer epoch, and causes stale commands to be rejected.

Real passwords, tokens, keys, credentials, sensitive prompts, and secret values MUST NOT appear in cards, prompts, conversations, incidents, evidence, logs, traces, telemetry, repositories, or shared environments. Production secrets resolve

A trusted local-only policy MAY display only explicitly non-secret, disposable bootstrap fixture values or test OTPs classified by trusted metadata. They MUST never reach remote repositories, shared logs, telemetry, evidence, deployment, sh

Artifacts and evidence MUST be encrypted, sensitivity-tiered, deduplicated, access-reviewed, quota-controlled, and governed by signed retention. Pilot retention is ninety days for operational recovery evidence and one year for approved deci

Every agent role receives daily exception and weekly trend views across scope adherence, correctness, evidence quality, normalized timeliness, handoff completeness, compliance, rework, recurrence, escaped defects, and role-specific outcomes

Results MUST show evidence, sample size, confidence, trend, and root-cause attribution among agent behavior, policy, workflow, resource, dependency, owner wait, and infrastructure. There MUST NOT be one composite leaderboard. Evaluation MUS
- Owner authority and signed policy;
- product and project isolation;
- work, artifact, environment, and service identity;
- source, workspace, release, and production integrity;
- production credentials and signing roots;
- evidence, incident, decision, and audit history;
- personal, customer, and regulated data;
- availability of guarded control components.
| Threat | Required control |
| Wrong-product or wrong-workspace action | Fail-closed product routing, exact bindings, exclusive leases |
| Stale worker or split-brain leader | Fencing epochs, single-active lease, stale-command rejection |
| Duplicate delivery or external effect | Idempotency keys, effect receipts, authoritative reconciliation |
| Privilege expansion during incident | Signed policy, short-lived exact capabilities, no self-expansion |
| Direct-write bypass | Sole guarded writer, credential isolation, continuous negative tests |
| Forged approval | Authenticated signed decision, exact binding, expiry, read-back |
| Secret leakage | Brokered execution, redaction and quarantine, rotation, no raw evidence values |
| Evidence tampering or deletion | Append-only ledger, immutable evidence, access review, tombstones |
| Alert or metric manipulation | Authenticated observations, deduplication, confidence and attribution |
| Product-change bypass through operations or security | Mandatory Flow 1 re-entry before material mutation |
| Retirement destroys needed data or consumers | Exact plan binding, legal-hold veto, staged proof, independent closure |
| Supply-chain or signing compromise | Immutable provenance, bill of materials, hardware-backed signing, rotation and revocation |
An implementation MUST NOT activate enforcement until all applicable tests pass:
1. wrong-product brief rejection before card creation;
2. wrong project, workspace, environment, artifact, or service binding denial;
3. duplicate command replay returns original result;
4. changed payload under existing idempotency key is rejected;
5. lost heartbeat with valid progress and valid heartbeat with stalled progress;
6. expired lease, stale fencing epoch, never-started run, duplicate wake, and superseded update;
7. resource wait persistence, fair wake-up, starvation escalation, and hold-resume exact membership;
8. Recovery Executor forbidden commit, merge, deployment, policy, and owner-decision actions;
9. partial external effect reconciliation before retry;
10. two sealed independent reviews and incomplete-lens Gatekeeper rejection;
11. material change invalidates review and approval evidence;
12. incompatible plugin, Executor, policy, or host activation fails closed;
13. build-once identity and rebuild invalidation;
14. production deployment without exact current Owner approval is rejected;
15. progressive pause and deterministic rollback routing;
16. secret value absent from prompts, cards, evidence, logs, and telemetry;
17. operational material-change bypass is rejected before effect;
18. security case entry, least disclosure, exact command, closure, and explicit hand-back;
19. backup restoration meets recovery objectives and integrity checks;
20. retirement blocked by legal hold, unknown consumer, active credential, residual traffic, failed deletion, or unresolved obligation;
21. direct persistence credential and direct-write bypass tests;
22. control-plane failover reconciliation and stale-leader rejection;
23. evidence retention, legal hold, backup expiry, and tombstone behavior;
24. owner brief preserves verdict, impact, risk, and next decision while omitting implementation noise;
25. metrics cannot automatically mutate roles, authority, dispatch, capability, or card state.
The implementation MAY enter these stages only in order:
1. observe-only Watchdog and classifier;
2. dry-run guarded command recommendations;
3. enforced Flow 1 routing and direct-write denial;
4. Flow 2 R0 only;
5. Flow 2 allowlisted R1 after evidence gate;
6. Flow 3 non-production artifact and promotion controls;
7. owner-authorized production release after full release gate;
8. Flow 4 observation and support classification;
9. preauthorized narrow operational commands;
10. owner-authorized retirement after restoration and legal-hold tests.

Each stage requires explicit kill criteria, rollback criteria, evidence, independent review, and Owner activation approval bound to the implemented version and signed policy. Broader classes require a new owner-approved policy version.

Every normative rule MUST map to one or more canonical discussion decisions and one or more conformance tests. The implementation plan MUST NOT weaken a normative rule. A discovered ambiguity or contradiction returns to specification review
Changes to product authority, recovery class, reviewer lens, protected subsystem, resource precedence, security command, production approval, retention, or retirement policy require:
1. evidence-backed PM proposal;
2. Product Secretary scope and completeness check;
3. explicit Owner approval;
4. new signed policy or specification version;
5. migration, replay, compatibility, negative, and rollback tests;
6. auditable activation and revocation records.

This draft is intended for owner review. Approval of this document authorizes only creation of a separate implementation plan. It does not authorize implementation, installation, migration, deployment, secret provisioning, policy activation
